title: Next-day fuel price commitment, MyFuel NT (Northern Territory)
summary: From 20 April 2026 NT fuel retailers must report, between 8.30 am and 2 pm, the price that will apply for the next 24 hours from 6 am, and may only cut it within that period.

instruments.title: Consumer Affairs and Fair Trading (Fuel Retailers) Amendment Regulations 2026
instruments.provisions: reg 5 replaced: reporting for MyFuel NT

commenced.what: Next-day price reporting replaced real-time reporting

direction_rationale: Requiring retailers to set tomorrow's price the day before, with cuts but no rises allowed within the day (as in WA), removes the sudden jumps that start retail price cycles; the effect on average margins is ambiguous, because a posted price is also a commitment rivals can match.
comparison: Reporting-only states (NSW, QLD, SA, TAS); WA (next-day rule since 2001) as an always-treated benchmark
confounders: crude oil and terminal gate price movements

verified.notes: Read on the NT register (as-made PDF): made 17 April 2026, commence 20 April 2026.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Retailers must post tomorrow's price the day before and may only cut it during the day, as in Perth. It ends sudden price jumps, but restricting price changes and publishing commitments in advance can make prices easier to match; Perth's experience does not show a clear fall in average margins.

marks.reason: Limits when retailers can change prices, and advance commitments make rivals' prices easy to match.
Retailers must set and report the next day's price within a daily window.
